description: Neither behavioral-spec.md's Ground Truth section nor verification-architecture.md's concrete refactor pseudocode preserves (or even mentions) the REAL existing `if a.live:` gate at post_reel.py:121 that currently scopes the before-snapshot read. In the REAL current file (verified by direct Read, /Users/anicca/.claude/skills/ig-reels-poster/scripts/post_reel.py:119-124), the single unstabilized read at :123 (`res["_before_reels"] = ev(...)`) only ever executes when `a.live` is True -- it is nested three levels deep inside `if a.live:` (:121). When `a.live` is False (the file's own documented DEFAULT: line 19's docstring reads 'default = dry (loads video, fills caption, stops before シェア, discards)'), NO before-snapshot is taken at all, and the composer opens immediately. behavioral-spec.md's Ground Truth section (lines 42-44) cites ':123' as 'THE actual root-cause single-read site... This is THE site REQ-001 fixes' WITHOUT ever mentioning the surrounding `if a.live:` conditional that determines whether this code even runs. verification-architecture.md's concrete refactor pseudocode (lines 39-50) is textually explicit that it removes this scoping: it opens with an unconditional `before = stabilize_reads(...)` followed immediately by `if not before["stable"]: ...abort...`, with the comment 'the composer/upload/share flow is now GATED on `before["stable"]`' (verification-architecture.md line 35) -- stated with NO qualification that this gating only applies when `a.live` is True. Read literally (and there is no other reading available -- the pseudocode is the ONLY concrete implementation guidance given), an implementer would remove the `if a.live:` wrapper entirely and run the new stabilize_reads call unconditionally for EVERY invocation of post_reel.py, including dry runs. This is a real, previously-undetected behavior change with two distinct harms, neither addressed by any requirement: (1) every dry run (used for manual/dev validation of the composer/caption flow, per the file's own docstring, and NOT gated away by run.sh, which always passes --live per run.sh:88 -- so dry mode is exclusively a manual/testing invocation path today) would newly incur ~10s of extra browser navigation+polling latency it never had before; (2) dry runs would gain an entirely NEW failure/abort mode -- if the before-snapshot fails to stabilize (an explicitly anticipated possible outcome per REQ-002), the dry run now ABORTS with `outcome="failed"` and never even reaches the composer, even though a dry run structurally CANNOT cause the false-positive-post/duplicate-post harm this whole feature exists to prevent (dry runs never reach the live-share code path at post_reel.py:170+, gated separately by the SAME `a.live` flag at line 165). Precedent within this same spec: FIND-003 (iteration-3) already established the principle that composer/share flow gating on `before["stable"]` must be carefully scoped to avoid unintended side effects on paths that were previously ungated -- but FIND-003's fix only addressed the LIVE path's duplicate-post risk; it never considered (and no subsequent iteration considered) whether the SAME new gate, as literally specified, also silently swallows the existing `a.live` conditional for the DRY path. No requirement (REQ-001 through REQ-004) states whether the new before-snapshot/stabilize/abort logic should remain scoped to `if a.live:` (zero regression for dry mode, matching the Ground Truth's own 'no regression for X' pattern used elsewhere in this spec, e.g. REQ-006's citation of `_instance_paths.sh`'s 'Unset ANICCA_INSTANCE => identical to the pre-split paths (zero regression)') or apply unconditionally as a deliberate, called-out design decision -- and if the latter, no proof obligation (PROP-001 through PROP-011) tests dry-mode behavior at all; every PROP-00x test in verification-architecture.md exercises either the pure functions in isolation or the live (`a.live=True`) path exclusively.
